claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria (c.185–c.254) was a Christian theologian, presbyter, and head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria before founding a school in Caesarea.
The Homilies on Luke were preached in Caesarea, probably between 234 and 240, to a mixed audience of catechumens and faithful believers.
The work consists of thirty‑nine short sermons, each treating about six verses of Luke and lasting roughly eight to twelve minutes.
The first thirty‑three homilies cover Luke chapters 1‑4, while the remaining six address passages from chapters 10‑20.
Only the Latin translation made by Jerome survives in full, preserving thirty‑nine homilies, while several hundred Greek fragments also exist.
These homilies are the only extant patristic commentary on Luke’s Gospel before Ambrose’s late‑fourth‑century exposition.
Homilies 1‑20 constitute the only surviving pre‑Nicene commentary on the Infancy Narrative of Luke.
The homilies are important because they reveal Origen’s method of starting with a literal reading of the text and then moving to spiritual interpretation, a model for early Christian exegesis.
